facts.claim: OAMS roll thruster No. 8 short-circuited and stuck open while the crew maneuvered the docked Gemini-Agena
After undocking Gemini rolled, pitched and yawed even more rapidly, reaching a roll rate of about one rotation per second
Armstrong shut down the OAMS and used the nose re-entry control system, all 16 RCS thrusters, using about 75 percent of the RCS fuel; mission rules then required an early landing
Eight 25 lbf OAMS attitude thrusters sat around the aft end of the adapter
Gemini was about 5.7 to 5.8 m long with a 3.05 m adapter base; the Agena target was 1.52 m wide and about 7.9 m long with its docking adapter
On 16 March 1966 Gemini 8 made the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit with an Agena target vehicle
Thruster circuits were changed so a single fault could be isolated
The peak roll rate is reported at about 296 degrees per second
